goalbuddy_receipt_v1.rationale: The backend is a compact monolith: TaskInput validation, preflight, run creation/persistence, Git locking/status/diff/allowedPaths/checkpoint enforcement, prompting, and run APIs are in server/index.ts; integration coverage is in server/index.test.ts. Baselines are green. One backend TDD package can add read-only GoalBuddy selection and exact mapping, carry external linkage through the existing run path, validate a versioned receipt contract, and atomically emit a separate receipt beside run.json without UI or scheduler duplication.

worker_package.objective: Using TDD, implement the backend GoalBuddy Bridge V1 vertical slice: read and validate an operator-selected state.yaml with exactly one active task, map it into an Orchestrator TaskInput preview, carry immutable GoalBuddy linkage through the existing preflight/createRun/execute/persist path, and atomically write a schema-valid GoalReceiptEnvelopeV1 JSON beside the run record after task execution.
stop_if: The slice requires UI, queue files, or files outside allowed_files.
The bridge cannot reuse the existing preflight/createRun/execute/persist and Git safety path.
Any design would write to or advance the selected GoalBuddy state.yaml, select another GoalBuddy task, or enable automatic commits.
Goal/task/repo/run linkage or failure/cancellation receipt semantics cannot be represented without a material product decision.
A goal-owned verification command fails twice for the same unexplained reason.
